subject: AuroraBank SIG follow-up: SDLC control clarifications
messages:
From: Alyssa Mendoza <alyssa.mendoza@aurorabank.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: security-assessments@aurorabank.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: AuroraBank SIG follow-up: SDLC control clarifications

Irene —

Thanks for the documents you submitted last week. We're running through the SIG artifacts and have a few follow-ups specifically tied to your Secure SDLC responses. To close the section on code review, CI/CD controls, secrets management, and change management we need the following from Redwood: 

- PR approval matrix (who can approve what, minimum reviewer counts) and where that is enforced (policy vs automation).
- Sanitized CI logs showing a representative release build (RELEASE-20270501 or closest) including job names and timestamps.
- Evidence of ephemeral credential rotation/proof-of-rotation for the CI runner role that deploys to staging (screenshots or rotation log snippet with timestamps).
- Chronology of the change approval for RELEASE-20270501 (ticket references, approvals, sign-offs).
- The emergency rollback/runbook that was used as an internal reference for hotfixes.

We prefer redacted artifacts (remove commit bodies with PII) but keep reviewer IDs and timestamps. Can you confirm what you can provide by EOD Wednesday?

Best,
Alyssa
Alyssa Mendoza
Senior Assessor, AuroraBank Security
alyssa.mendoza@aurorabank.com
From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Mendoza <alyssa.mendoza@aurorabank.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AuroraBank SIG follow-up: SDLC control clarifications

Alyssa —

Thanks for the clear list. We'll assemble a sanitized package. Quick clarifications so we send exactly what you need: 

1) For PR enforcement: do you need the GitHub branch-protection policy file + a short note on how it's enforced by our CI gate, or would a CSV export of the PR reviewer matrix (role -> approval capability) suffice?
2) CI logs: we'll provide a sanitized tarball with job names and timestamps; do you need raw logs or a curated timeline?
3) Ephemeral rotation: we can provide a timestamped rotation event and the agent service audit entry (redacted keys). Is a single sampled rotation enough, or do you want the last 90 days of rotations?
4) Change chronology: we'll export the ticket thread and approval steps for RELEASE-20270501 (SUP-2345).
5) Runbook: we'll attach the current emergency-rollback PDF and mark the sections used during the May rollout.

We expect to have the initial package ready by Wednesday EOD (2027-05-12) and can push items earlier if you need anything sooner. Attaching a proposed artifact list below — if that maps to your ask I'll begin the export.

Proposed artifacts we will attach:
- redwood_pr_approval_matrix.pdf (policy + matrix)
- ci-logs-sanitized.tar.gz (curated jobs + timestamps)
- ephemeral-rotation-sample.txt (rotation audit snippet)
- change-approval-chronology-RELEASE-20270501.csv (ticket timeline)
- emergency-rollback-runbook.pdf

Regards,
Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Alyssa Mendoza <alyssa.mendoza@aurorabank.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AuroraBank SIG follow-up: SDLC control clarifications

Irene / Alyssa —

Quick operational notes to accompany the package: 
- PR enforcement is both policy and automation: branch-protection prevents merges without 1+ approver and passing required CI statuses (see attached policy in the matrix).
- The CI job names you should expect in the log bundle: build, unit-test, static-analysis, integration-test, deploy-staging, deploy-prod. We'll keep the job names and timestamps intact and redact sensitive env output.
- RELEASE-20270501 maps to SUP-2345 in our tracker; the ticket contains the change proposal, design review, and the final sign-off by the release manager.

I'll pull the sanitized CI logs and drop to the shared auditor folder.

Jonas Weber
Senior Engineering Manager, Platform
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, Alyssa Mendoza <alyssa.mendoza@aurorabank.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AuroraBank SIG follow-up: SDLC control clarifications

Alyssa / Irene —

Uploading the sanitized artifacts now. A couple of technical notes to validate the artifacts you will receive: 

- ci-logs-sanitized.tar.gz: contains the curated timeline for RELEASE-20270501. Log entries are sanitized to remove stack traces that reference internal asset names; reviewer IDs (github handles) and timestamps are preserved. Example log header: 
  [2027-05-01T02:14:33Z] job=deploy-staging status=passed runner=ci-runner-07

- ephemeral-rotation-sample.txt: this is an audit entry from our credential manager showing a rotation event for the ci-runner service account. Format (redacted):
  rotation_id: rot-7c3b
  rotated_at: 2027-04-30T23:48:10Z
  rotated_by: ops-bot
  previous_key_id: [REDACTED]
  new_key_id: [REDACTED]

- change-approval-chronology-RELEASE-20270501.csv: CSV columns are [timestamp, actor, action, ticket_ref, note]. We include the reviewer handle and the release manager sign-off row.

Attachments uploaded to: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/aurorabank/sdlc-evidence/ (read-only link for your team). For the auditor record we also linked SUP-2345 and JIRA-RUN-9872 in the export manifest.

Please confirm receipt and whether you require an expanded rotation history.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Alyssa Mendoza <alyssa.mendoza@aurorabank.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 12:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AuroraBank SIG follow-up: SDLC control clarifications

Thanks — receiving the upload link now. A few small follow-ups: 

- Could you provide the commit hash for the deploy (or the canonical build id) used in the RELEASE-20270501 logs so we can cross-reference the PR thread?
- For the ephemeral rotation sample, please include the agent that initiated the rotation (ops-bot is fine) plus a short note confirming whether the rotation is fully automated or requires human approval.
- For PR review evidence: we need a screenshot or exported thread showing reviewer comments and the approval actions (timestamps + reviewer handles). A redacted export is fine if it preserves the reviewer handles and timestamps.

If you can add those items to the same folder by EOD Wednesday we'll be able to mark the Secure SDLC section as resolved.

Best,
Alyssa
From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Mendoza <alyssa.mendoza@aurorabank.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AuroraBank SIG follow-up: SDLC control clarifications

Alyssa —

Thanks for the quick review. We've added the extra artifacts you requested to the shared folder: 

- redwood_pr_approval_matrix.pdf (policy + enforcement notes) [attachment]
- ci-logs-sanitized.tar.gz (includes build id: build-20270501-7cf3a2 and commit hash: 9f1c3d2) [attachment]
- ephemeral-rotation-sample.txt (rotation initiated by ops-bot; automated rotation scheduled daily, manual approval required for HSM key changes) [attachment]
- change-approval-chronology-RELEASE-20270501.csv (includes SUP-2345 -> final sign-off by @release_mgr at 2027-05-01T03:12:45Z) [attachment]
- emergency-rollback-runbook.pdf (runbook with annotated sections used in May rollout) [attachment]
- pr-review-thread-export.html (redacted thread preserving reviewer handles and timestamps) [attachment]

Links: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/aurorabank/sdlc-evidence/ (read-only). Tickets referenced in the package: SUP-2345, JIRA-RUN-9872.

If you'd like a quick walkthrough of the artifacts, Jonas and I can run a 30-minute screen-share tomorrow morning. Otherwise, please confirm this closes the Secure SDLC portion.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
